core_obligations: Reduce to invariants: by the Poincare-Birkhoff-Witt theorem it is enough to show that the space of invariants of the adjoint action of a[u] on its supersymmetric algebra is trivial (proof lines 1247-1252).

Expand an invariant in the top degree: let A be an invariant and d the maximal degree in which A involves the basis elements f_1 u^d, ..., f_K u^d, and write A as a polynomial in those top-degree elements with coefficients free of them, allowing m_p > 1 only for even basis elements (proof lines 1254-1276).

Extract the top component of the invariance equation: the component of ad(f_p u)(A) = 0 involving the elements f_1 u^{d+1}, ..., f_K u^{d+1} vanishes, which yields the linear system (ad) with the sign h'_q defined in the proof (proof lines 1278-1315).

Compare two linear systems: the elements (m'_q + 1) f_q (-1)^{h'_q} again form a homogeneous basis of a, so by triviality of the centre of a the corresponding system on w_1, ..., w_K has only the zero solution; comparing it with (ad) makes every top-degree coefficient A_{m'_1 ... m'_q+1 ... m'_K} vanish, hence d = 0 and A lies in C (proof lines 1317-1343).
proof_roadmap: Pass from the centre of the enveloping algebra to the invariants of the adjoint action by PBW, and set up the top-degree expansion of an invariant (proof lines 1247-1276).

Read the top-degree part of the invariance equation as a linear system, compare it with the system expressing triviality of the centre of a, and conclude that the top degree is zero (proof lines 1278-1343).
difficulty_reason: The proposition is about a Lie superalgebra a with trivial centre and claims that the centre of the enveloping algebra U(a[u]) of its polynomial current algebra is also trivial, that is equal to the scalars (statement lines 1239-1244). The proof passes to the invariants of the adjoint action on the supersymmetric algebra by the Poincare-Birkhoff-Witt theorem, takes an invariant A of maximal degree d in the generators f_i u^d, and expands it in the top-degree monomials (proof lines 1247-1276). The step that carries the content is the comparison at the end: the top-degree part of the invariance equation is a linear system whose coefficient matrix is the same as the one expressing triviality of the centre of a, after replacing the basis by (m'_q + 1) f_q (-1)^{h'_q}; triviality of the centre of a forces only the zero solution, and the coefficients of A in top degree therefore die one by one (proof lines 1317-1343). The degree argument then collapses d to zero. The whole proof is self-contained apart from the cited PBW reduction, so H2.
